description: A synthetic library of 21 research papers on linear attention, long-term memory, KV cache compression, Kolmogorov-Arnold networks, retrieval-augmented generation and mixture-of-experts, three of them long (two surveys and a thesis); fictional, generated by `shodh-eval synth-papers`

cases.question: What does the gate alpha_t do in the gated delta rule?

sources.passage: the gate alpha_t decays the whole state before the delta update writes the new association

cases.question: What is the state update equation of LUMEN?

sources.passage: S_t = alpha_t S_{t-1} (I - beta_t k_t k_t^T) + beta_t v_t k_t^T

cases.question: What chunk size does LUMEN use for chunk-wise parallel training?

sources.passage: we use a chunk size of 64 tokens

cases.question: Why is the gated delta rule a form of online gradient descent?

sources.passage: one step of online gradient descent with learning rate beta_t on the loss

cases.question: Why does softmax attention cost O(n^2) in the sequence length?

sources.passage: Softmax attention compares every query with every key

cases.question: What limitation of LUMEN do its authors acknowledge?

sources.passage: exact copying of long spans remains weaker than in softmax attention

cases.question: How does TIDE measure surprise?

sources.passage: surprise is the gradient of the associative loss with respect to the memory parameters

cases.question: Why does TIDE use momentum when it updates its memory?

sources.passage: momentum carries the surprise of earlier tokens

cases.question: How does TIDE remove old information from its memory?

sources.passage: Old information is removed by a data-dependent forgetting gate

cases.question: In which ways can the TIDE memory be added to a model?

sources.passage: We compare memory as context, memory as gate and memory as layer

cases.question: What loss does the TIDE memory minimise at test time?

sources.passage: loss(M; x_t) = || M(k_t) - v_t ||^2

cases.question: What is test-time training and why use it for memory?

sources.passage: Test-time training offers a third option: treat memorization as learning

cases.question: Why does SQUEEZE quantize keys per channel?

sources.passage: a few key channels carry outliers whose magnitude is ten to fifty times the median

cases.question: How many recent tokens does SQUEEZE keep in full precision?

sources.passage: the most recent 128 tokens stay in full precision

cases.question: What quantization group size does SQUEEZE use?

sources.passage: We use a group size of 32 for both keys and values

cases.question: How large is the KV cache of a 7B model serving 16 requests at 32K tokens?

sources.passage: the cache needs 256 GB in half precision

cases.question: Why does HARBOR always keep the first tokens of the sequence?

sources.passage: because they act as attention sinks

cases.question: How does HARBOR rank tokens to find heavy hitters?

sources.passage: HARBOR ranks tokens by this accumulated attention score

cases.question: When does KV cache eviction with HARBOR fail?

sources.passage: Questions about a detail that received little attention early in a long document are the main failure case

cases.question: Which theorem are Kolmogorov-Arnold networks based on?

sources.passage: KANs are based on the Kolmogorov-Arnold representation theorem

cases.question: Where do the learnable activation functions sit in a KAN?

sources.passage: the learnable activation functions sit on edges and the nodes only sum their inputs

cases.question: How does KANDLE refine its spline grid during training?

sources.passage: KANDLE uses grid extension from G = 5 to G = 20 in three stages

cases.question: What spline order do KANDLE's edge functions use?

sources.passage: The spline has order k = 3

cases.question: How does ORBIT make rotary position encoding work with linear attention?

sources.passage: ORBIT applies the rotation to queries and keys before the feature map and stores rotated keys in the state

cases.question: What does \mathbf{S}_t denote in the ORBIT paper?

sources.passage: is the state matrix after token t

cases.question: What taxonomy does the survey use to group efficient sequence models?

sources.passage: We group efficient sequence models into three families according to what they change

cases.question: What open problems remain for efficient long-context models?

sources.passage: We see four open problems

cases.question: What does Ripple do to the KV cache?

sources.passage: lowering the precision of tokens as they age from eight bits to two

cases.question: What WikiText perplexity does LUMEN reach at 1.3B parameters?
How much faster than FlashAttention-2 is LUMEN's training at 16K context?

sources.passage: 2.3 times the FlashAttention-2 baseline

cases.question: What LongRecall accuracy does TIDE reach at 16K tokens?

sources.passage: TIDE as context 93.0 71.3 60.8 48.2

cases.question: What LongSuite score does SQUEEZE keep with 2-bit quantization?

sources.passage: SQUEEZE 2 5.3x 3.1x 47.2

cases.question: What RMSE does KANDLE reach on the Feynman equations benchmark?
Which paper proposed the gated delta rule for linear attention?

sources.passage: We present LUMEN, a linear attention layer whose state is updated by a gated delta rule

cases.question: Which paper introduced per-channel quantization of keys in the KV cache?

sources.passage: Keys are quantized per channel and values per token

cases.question: Which paper uses surprise to decide what a memory should store at test time?

sources.passage: so that it memorizes the tokens that surprise it most

cases.question: Which paper evicts KV cache entries by their accumulated attention?

sources.passage: HARBOR is a training-free eviction policy

cases.question: Which paper adds rotary position encoding to chunk-wise linear attention?

sources.passage: We present ORBIT, which applies rotary position encoding to the queries and keys of chunk-wise linear attention

cases.question: What work does the ORBIT paper cite for rotary position embedding?

sources.passage: Rotary position embedding for transformers

cases.question: How do SQUEEZE and HARBOR shrink the KV cache in different ways?

sources.passage: Quantization reduces the size of every cached entry but keeps every entry
keeps only a fixed budget of the key-value cache

cases.question: Can KV cache quantization and eviction be combined, and how much memory does that save?

sources.passage: reduces cache memory by 12 times with a loss of 1.5 points
the two can be applied together

cases.question: How do LUMEN and TIDE differ in the way they write to memory?

sources.passage: The delta rule writes the difference between the new value and the value currently retrieved for the key
the memory is trained online to minimise the reconstruction error of the pair

cases.question: What approaches in my papers reduce the memory needed for long-context inference?

sources.passage: reduces KV cache memory by 5.3 times
keeps only a fixed budget of the key-value cache
PRISM projects every cached key onto a rank-64 subspace
SENTINEL keeps the cache in host memory

cases.question: Which methods train linear attention with a chunk-wise parallel form?

sources.passage: We split the sequence into chunks and compute each chunk's contribution with matrix multiplications
The output of a query combines an intra-chunk term computed with masked attention and an inter-chunk term read from the state

cases.question: How do these models forget or drop old context?

sources.passage: the gate alpha_t decays the whole state before the delta update writes the new association
Old information is removed by a data-dependent forgetting gate
When the cache is full the token with the lowest score outside the sinks and the recent window is evicted

cases.question: How well do fixed-state models recall facts in long inputs compared with attention?

sources.passage: closes most of the recall gap that plain linear attention leaves
Linear attention 58.4 31.7 12.9 4.1

cases.question: Which KV cache methods need no retraining of the model?

sources.passage: a tuning-free method that stores the cache in two bits per number
HARBOR is a training-free eviction policy

cases.question: Which papers describe a recurrent state updated token by token?

sources.passage: This recurrence has constant memory per token
the memory is trained online to minimise the reconstruction error of the pair
the state carries keys rotated by their absolute position

cases.question: How many entries of each feature vector does VESPER keep?

sources.passage: VESPER keeps only the 16 largest entries of each feature vector

cases.question: What WikiText perplexity does VESPER reach at 760M parameters?

sources.passage: VESPER reaches a WikiText perplexity of 18.35

cases.question: By what factor does TESSERA expand the state of each head?

sources.passage: TESSERA expands the state of every head by a factor of four

cases.question: How much does TESSERA improve MQAR accuracy?

sources.passage: TESSERA lifts MQAR accuracy from 61.0 to 83.5

cases.question: How many memory slots does CAIRN write each token into?

sources.passage: CAIRN writes each token into the two memory slots whose keys are closest to it

cases.question: How many summaries does MEANDER replay before answering?

sources.passage: replays the 8 most similar summaries before answering a question

cases.question: How much does episodic replay improve BookQA accuracy?

sources.passage: Replay improves accuracy on the synthetic BookQA benchmark from 39.2% to 57.8%

cases.question: What rank does PRISM project cached keys to?

sources.passage: PRISM projects every cached key onto a rank-64 subspace

cases.question: How much does PRISM reduce KV cache memory when combined with quantization?

sources.passage: by 9.8 times when combined with two-bit quantization

cases.question: How does SENTINEL decide which KV cache pages to prefetch?

sources.passage: prefetches the pages that the previous layer's queries attended to most

cases.question: What context length can SENTINEL serve on a single 24 GB GPU?

sources.passage: SENTINEL serves 1M-token contexts on a single 24 GB GPU

cases.question: What does RIVULET use on a KAN's edges instead of B-splines?

sources.passage: truncated Fourier series of 12 terms

cases.question: What error does QUARRY reach on the Poisson equation?

sources.passage: relative L2 error of 3.4e-4

cases.question: How does QUARRY impose boundary conditions?

sources.passage: Boundary conditions in QUARRY are imposed exactly

cases.question: What does BEACON do with sentences whose citation does not support them?

sources.passage: drops sentences whose cited passage does not entail them

cases.question: How much does BEACON improve citation precision?

sources.passage: BEACON raises citation precision from 61.4% to 88.0%

cases.question: What constant does FATHOM use in reciprocal rank fusion?

sources.passage: reciprocal rank fusion using a constant of 60

cases.question: How many experts does CONFLUX route each token to?

sources.passage: CONFLUX routes every token to 2 of 64 experts

cases.question: How much training compute does CONFLUX need to match a dense model?

sources.passage: with 31% of its training compute

cases.question: When does ESTUARY merge two experts?

sources.passage: cosine similarity above 0.9

cases.question: How many experts remain after ESTUARY merges them?

sources.passage: reduces the number of experts from 64 to 41

cases.question: How does the thesis define a memory mechanism?

sources.passage: a memory mechanism is any component that carries information from one token to a later one without recomputing it

cases.question: What is the central claim of the thesis on memory mechanisms?

sources.passage: write policies matter more than memory size

cases.question: How does the KV cache compression survey divide the methods it covers?

sources.passage: divide KV cache compression into token-level, precision-level and dimension-level methods

cases.question: How large is the key-value cache of a 70B model at 128K tokens?

sources.passage: exceeds 300 GB in half precision

cases.question: Which paper routes each token to 2 of 64 experts?

sources.passage: CONFLUX routes every token to 2 of 64 experts

cases.question: Which paper replaces B-splines with Fourier series in a Kolmogorov-Arnold network?

sources.passage: RIVULET replaces the B-splines of a KAN with truncated Fourier series

cases.question: Which paper offloads the KV cache to host memory?

sources.passage: SENTINEL keeps the cache in host memory

cases.question: How do CONFLUX and ESTUARY change the experts of a mixture-of-experts model?

sources.passage: CONFLUX routes every token to 2 of 64 experts
ESTUARY merges experts whose weight vectors have a cosine similarity above 0.9

cases.question: How do BEACON and FATHOM improve retrieval-augmented generation?

sources.passage: BEACON asks the generator to cite a passage for every sentence
FATHOM fuses a BM25 ranking and a dense ranking

cases.question: What functions do RIVULET and KANDLE put on the edges of a KAN?

sources.passage: truncated Fourier series of 12 terms
Each edge function is a cubic B-spline plus a residual SiLU term

sources.passage: CAIRN writes each token into the two memory slots whose keys are closest to it
surprise is the gradient of the associative loss with respect to the memory parameters

sources.passage: so a state write touches a small fraction of the state
TESSERA expands the state of every head by a factor of four
